catalog_quote: [JIPA 2021, 'Tone and word stress':] Northern Tepehuan is a tonal language with a single phonological tone: the high tone H. ... the H tone is culminative, i.e., it occurs at most once in a phonological word ... Stress is predictable from the size and the tonal pattern of the word. Stress falls on the first syllable in disyllabic words – regardless of lexical tone or vowel duration as shown in (4) and (5) above – and on the second syllable in phonologically toneless words with three or more syllables, as in /ipuːrai/ [iˈpuːrɛi] ‘dress’ or /nakasɨrai/ [naˈqasɨrɛi] ‘scorpion’. However, when a H tone is phonologically specified in the first syllable and the word has three or more syllables, the stress always falls in the H syllable, as in /úːridɨ/ [ˈúːʎiɟɨ] ‘his maternal grandmother’, in contrast, for instance, with /iːbɨxi/ [iːˈbɨxi] ‘he/she breathes’, and /taːtasai/ [taːˈtasəi] ‘he/she s…
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Northern Tepehuan is not in the catalog. The one works with stress in the title (Glottolog 669887, author-less) is Kim, Michael Jinhwa 1997, WCCFL 15: 257-272, a metrical reanalysis of Bascom's data claiming tone is predictable from stress; this search of works with stress in the title instead turned up and read two open first-hand sources by Carlos Gil Burgoin: AMP 9 (2021), which gives an explicit rule (stress never final; disyllables initial; longer words: first heavy syllable, else second syllable; L-toned initial long vowels repel stress; NON-FINALITY >> IAMBIC-RHYTHM >> STRESS-TO-WEIGHT) with acoustic backing, and the CLECM 7 (2020) critical bibliography, which documents that Bascom 1982: 272 called stress non-contrastive and freely fluctuating, that Woo 1970 does not treat stress, and that Kim 1997 works from Bascom's data. Bascom 1982 (SIL sketch, now could not be reached by automated download/print), Bascom 1959 and Woo 1970 (paywalled DOIs) remain unread; Bascom 1982 is the high-priority acquisition. Recommended new record: weight-sensitive initial-window stress, deciding source Gil Burgoin 2021 sec. 5.

new_statements.rule_in_words: One stress per word, never on the final syllable. Disyllables are always stressed on the first syllable regardless of weight or pitch. In words of three or more syllables, stress falls on the first heavy syllable (long vowel, consonant coda or glide coda), otherwise on the second syllable ([ˈúːrugi] 'bird', [ˈtáʃkaʎi] 'tortilla' vs. [baˈtópa] 'fish'). Suffixation of a light-light disyllable moves stress to the second syllable ([ˈúsù] > [ùˈsúdɨ̀]). Modelled as NON-FINALITY >> IAMBIC-RHYTHM >> STRESS-TO-WEIGHT.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned. The author assumes Hyman's culminativity (at most one stress per word, sec. 3) and describes a single prominence 'always in the first or second syllable' (p. 1).
new_statements.exceptions: (1) Suffixed forms of disyllables with the L.H pitch pattern (lexical L on the long first vowel) stress the second syllable although the first is heavy: [ˈbàːbá] + dɨ > [bàːˈbádɨ̀] 'grandfather.3s' (sec. 5.2). (2) Some morphologically simple polysyllables have an unstressed initial long vowel: [iːˈbɨ́hɨj] 'breath', [taːˈtámwi] 'tooth' (sec. 5.3). Both are attributed to a lexical low tone repelling stress (*ALIGN(HEAD/LOW), sec. 6). Note that Bascom 1982: 272 had instead claimed 'Stress is noncontrastive. It is freely fluctuation [sic] in many words.'
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in a tonal language (analysed as privative /L/; earlier work as H vs. L). Evidence: a 1200-entry lexical base, F0 measurements on 692 disyllabic tokens, two female speakers from Tupuri village, Baborigame, Chihuahua. Stress cued by an intonational H* on the stressed syllable except in L-toned words, where the pitch peak is on the following syllable. Bascom 1982 (grammar sketch, p. 272) and Bascom 2003 (draft grammar, sec. 0.1) give no placement rule; Gil Burgoin's 2021 JIPA Illustration (paywalled) is reported by its abstract to refine the rule (stress on the first syllable of disyllables, typically the second syllable of longer toneless words, aligned with a first-syllable H in 3+ syllable words).
new_statements.identity_note: Gil Burgoin's data come from two female speakers of the Tupuri village, Baborigame, Chihuahua, i.e. the Baborigame dialect, which Bascom 1982: 271 calls the larger of the two major dialects (the other is Nabogame). Bascom 1982/2003 and Bascom & Molina 1998 are also Baborigame. No separate Glottolog dialect code is known to me; the language-level code nort2959 applies.

new_statements.reading: Fixed, predictable, weight-sensitive stress confined to a left-edge two-syllable window and never final: disyllables initial; longer words stress the first heavy syllable (long vowel, consonant or glide coda; long vowels occur only in sigma-1) else the second syllable; a lexically L-toned initial long vowel repels stress to sigma-2. Same 'first heavy in a two-syllable window' shape as the catalog's Southeastern Tepehuan record (Willett 1991 / Reyes Taboada 2014). Coexists with a privative lexical L tone. First-hand data (Baborigame, two speakers, 1200-word base, acoustic measurements). Supersedes the older 'stress fluctuates freely / stress predicted from tone' lines attributed to Bascom 1959/1982.

sources.quote: Sobre el primero [el acento], Bascom señala que no es contrastivo y que fluctúa libremente (Bascom 1982: 272). [...] Kim (1997), en cambio, utiliza los datos de Bascom para mostrar que el tono es predecible a partir del acento y de la estructura métrica -aunque, vistos ciertos ejemplos, es dudoso-. [Translation: On the former (stress), Bascom states that it is not contrastive and fluctuates freely (Bascom 1982: 272). Kim (1997), by contrast, uses Bascom's data to show that tone is predictable from stress and metrical structure -though, given certain examples, this is doubtful.]
sources.note: Critical review, sec. 4.1 pp. 15-17: 'Sobre el primero [acento], Bascom señala que no es contrastivo y que fluctúa libremente (Bascom 1982: 272)'; Woo 1970 'Tampoco habla del acento'; Kim 1997 derives tone from stress and metrical structure 'aunque, vistos ciertos ejemplos, es dudoso'; Gil Burgoin & Carrillo 2019 is the first systematic stress/tone proposal.
